title: At the Airport
summary: A passenger checks in at the airport, asks about luggage, and finds the correct gate.
description: An elementary travel scenario covering check-in vocabulary: boarding pass, hand luggage, gate, departure time, and a short security question.

vocabulary.definition: the counter at an airport where you register for your flight
the card that lets you get on the plane
the small bag you carry with you on the plane
the act of leaving, especially on a flight
the door at an airport where you get on the plane

dialogue.text: Good morning. May I see your passport, please?
Here you are. I am flying to Berlin.
Thank you. Do you have any luggage to check in?
Yes, one suitcase. And I have this small bag as hand luggage.
Perfect. Please put the suitcase on the scale.
Sure. What is the departure time?
Your flight leaves at eleven thirty from gate B twelve.
And what time do I need to be at the gate?
Please be at the gate at least thirty minutes before departure.

questions.q: Where is the passenger flying to?
How many suitcases does the passenger check in?

trueFalse.statement: The passenger only has hand luggage.
trueFalse.explanation: The passenger checks in one suitcase and also has a hand-luggage bag.

trueFalse.statement: The flight leaves at eleven thirty.
trueFalse.explanation: The agent says 'Your flight leaves at eleven thirty from gate B twelve.'

teacherTips: Before listening, show a real boarding pass or print a sample so students recognise key fields (gate, seat, boarding time).
Practise 'May I see your passport, please?' and similar polite airport phrases as a fixed exchange.
Extension: students design their own airport role-play with check-in, security, and the gate.

es.title: En el aeropuerto
es.summary: Un pasajero hace el check-in en el aeropuerto, pregunta por el equipaje y encuentra la puerta de embarque correcta.
es.description: Un escenario de viaje elemental con vocabulario de facturación: boarding pass, hand luggage, gate, departure time, y una breve pregunta de seguridad.

vocabulary.definition: el mostrador del aeropuerto donde te registras para tu vuelo
la tarjeta que te permite subir al avión
la bolsa pequeña que llevas contigo en el avión
el acto de irse, especialmente en un vuelo
la puerta del aeropuerto donde subes al avión

trueFalse.statement: El pasajero solo lleva equipaje de mano.
trueFalse.explanation: El pasajero factura una maleta y también lleva una bolsa de mano.

trueFalse.statement: El vuelo sale a las once y media.
trueFalse.explanation: El agente dice 'Your flight leaves at eleven thirty from gate B twelve'.

teacherTips: Antes de escuchar, muestra una tarjeta de embarque real o imprime una de ejemplo para que los estudiantes reconozcan los campos clave (gate, seat, boarding time).
Practica 'May I see your passport, please?' y frases similares del aeropuerto como intercambio fijo.
Ampliación: los estudiantes diseñan su propio role-play de aeropuerto con facturación, seguridad y puerta de embarque.
